issues.legal_issue: An adverse order in an appeal may be modified to grant partial ejectment where the circumstances make the matter fit for settlement and modification is considered just to the parties.
material_facts: The order under appeal caused serious hardship to the appellant because land he had possessed had been sold and was unavailable to him.
The appellant had no other source of sustenance apart from the land in dispute.
The case had been pending for a long time.
Counsel fairly conceded, at the court's instance, that the court could pass any order it considered reasonable to do justice to the parties.
issues.conclusion: The Court modified the judgment under appeal and allowed the ejectment application in part, directing that six acres of the disputed land be allotted with regard to the nature and character of the soil.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on its assessment that the matter was pre-eminently fit for settlement and that a reasonable order was needed to do justice in light of the pressing circumstances, the serious hardship, the prolonged litigation, and counsel's concession. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

rule.if: appeal_from_adverse_order and appellant_faces_serious_hardship and no_other_sustenance_source and prolonged_litigation and counsel_accepts_reasonable_relief

predicates.appeal_from_adverse_order: The proceeding is an appeal from an order adverse to the appellant.
predicates.appellant_faces_serious_hardship: The appellant faces serious hardship because land previously possessed by the appellant is no longer available.
predicates.no_other_sustenance_source: The appellant has no other source of sustenance apart from the disputed land.
predicates.prolonged_litigation: The case has remained pending for a long time.
predicates.counsel_accepts_reasonable_relief: Counsel concedes that the court may pass an order it considers reasonable to do justice to the parties.
predicates.partial_ejectment_granted: The ejectment application is allowed in part.

issues.definition: When an appeal from an adverse order involves serious hardship, no other source of sustenance, prolonged litigation, and counsel's acceptance of reasonable relief, the output is that ejectment is granted in part.
